claim_text: Draft v3 · 3 August 2026 · Nari Nari Tribal Council · Biodiversity Conservation Trust · UNSW Centre for Ecosystem Science
The property covers 85,911 ha, of which 67,349 ha fall within the mapped vegetation census used throughout.
The assessment characterises the inundation regime and the vegetation cover response across the property over the full Landsat archive period, 1988 to 2023.
It is descriptive at property scale and does not attribute observed behaviour to particular management interventions, for reasons set out in Section 11.
The first is a whole-property census of every mapped cell, which establishes how flooding is organised and how cover responds to it (Section 7).
The second applies that framework to management units — paddocks, parts of paddocks, and monitoring sites — to ask whether management can be distinguished (Sections 8 to 10).
Landsat 5, 7, 8, 9 | Fractional cover — photosynthetic, non-photosynthetic and bare fractions; seasonal composites | Vegetation cover, 1988–2023
Landsat-derived water observations | Annual inundation occurrence | Flood frequency, 1988–2023
Property spatial data | 64 management zones with grazing treatment attribute | Management units
Ground monitoring network | 66 one-hectare plots | Independent reference; not merged with satellite results
All products are held on a common analysis grid in EPSG:8058 at 24.97 m.
Vegetation percentile surfaces are natively 30 m and were bilinearly resampled to that grid; inundation surfaces are natively 25 m and were resampled by nearest neighbour.

VERIFY  Sensor-specific processing — the fractional cover algorithm version, cross-sensor calibration between Landsat 5, 7, 8 and 9, and the treatment of the Landsat 7 scan-line failure after 2003 — is not described here and should be added from the producing code.
The analysis replaces the 66 monitoring plots with a census of every mapped cell.
The census comprises 1,080,157 cells, each carrying one flood-frequency value and a set of cover percentiles.
It covers 67,349.3 ha of the 85,910.8 ha property — 78.4% — the remainder being unmapped for vegetation community.
No inferential statistic in this assessment treats the cells as independent, and no confidence interval or p-value is computed on that basis.
Two further context strata (Floodplain Woodland and Forest, 86,375 cells; other minor units, 4,951 cells) are set aside as treed or minor and carry no headline result.

Inland Floodplain carries approximately 239,000 cells per band against approximately 25,000 for Aeolian, so any property-wide aggregate is dominated by Inland Floodplain unless explicitly area-weighted or reported per stratum.
Figure 2 shows the stratification across the property.

VERIFY  The rule dividing each community into low, mid and high bands — fixed flood-frequency thresholds, within-community terciles, or another rule — is not stated here and should be taken from the producing code.
Band membership is not comparable across communities if terciles were used.
Total vegetation cover is the sum of the photosynthetic and non-photosynthetic fractional cover bands, as a percentage of ground area.
The p-th percentile is the value below which p per cent of a set falls — the 5th percentile is exceeded by 95% of the set, the 50th is the median.
Percentiles are order statistics: read off the ranked values directly, with no model, no distributional assumption and no fitting.
A percentile is unaffected by the magnitude of extreme values, only by their rank.
Percentiles are reported as measured and never subtracted from one another to form a derived index.
The 5th percentile of a combined area is not the mean of the 5th percentiles of its parts, so percentiles are recomputed at each support rather than aggregated upward.
Two distinct 5th-percentile metrics are in use, differing in the axis along which the percentile is taken.
Spatial floor | 5th percentile of cover across the cells of a unit, within a single year | Across space, within a year | veg_p05_spatial
Temporal floor | 5th percentile of one cell's cover across the full record | Across time, within a cell | veg_p05
For Bala 29ca the two read 40.5% and 51.1% respectively.
Every unit-scale figure uses the spatial floor unless stated otherwise; the census percentile results of Section 7 use the temporal floor.

Trends are ordinary least squares slopes of the annual series against water year, in percentage points of cover per year.
A slope of +0.556 pp/yr indicates the floor rising by about half a percentage point annually, approximately 19 points across the 35-year record.
Correlation coefficients accompanying trends (reported as r) measure how consistently the series follows the fitted line, not how steep it is.
The water-adjusted trend removes the part attributable to inundation within the same unit, by first estimating that unit's own sensitivity to water and then taking the trend in the residual series.
For Bala 29ca the raw floor trend is +0.682 pp/yr, the within-paddock water slope is 0.414, and the water-adjusted trend is +0.556 pp/yr.
Approximately 81.6% of the raw improvement survives adjustment, so it is not principally a wet-period artefact.
